messages:
eric (pm): Quick sync — proposing a phased rollout for regional downgrade + burst-suppression routing for the new fallback behavior. Goal: avoid broad traffic spikes when model variants fall back to larger/higher-cost pools and ensure graceful degradation during regional capacity pressure. Plan below, feedback welcome.

alina: high-level looks good. can you call out SDK flag name and client-side behavior? we need a deterministic hashing key to keep cohorts stable.

eric (pm): yes — flag = `rlw.regional_fallback_v2` (SDK exposure: boolean + rollout config). client behavior: if flag=false, clients use default routing. if true, client will attach `routing_cohort_id` derived from user_id (sha1 % 1000).

jess: from SRE POV: we need a guardrail on request amplification. if fallback causes CPU/GPU oversubscription, instantly cut to holdback. propose these telemetry thresholds: 5xx rate > 2% OR p99 latency increase > 30% for 5m window => auto-shred to holdback. also require a manual override kill-switch per-region.

mike: sketching the rollout buckets I used in the prototype:

```
rollout: {
  regions: ["us-west-2","us-east-1","eur-west-1"],
  cohorts: [1,5,20,100], // percent
  sequence: ["us-west-2:1","us-east-1:1","us-west-2:5","eur-west-1:1","us-west-2:20","us-east-1:5","global:100"],
  holdback: 5, // percent global reserve for immediate fallback
  min_sample_per_cohort: 1000
}
```

alina: min_sample_per_cohort=1000 — what's our telemetry look like for low-volume tenants? we need per-tenant opt-out and a pass for customers on dedicated capacity.

eric (pm): agreed — dedicated customers get an explicit opt-out API and we won't touch routing. for low-volume tenants, we'll only include them if they exceed 200 requests/day for the feature; otherwise they're routed to default.

sam: telemetry keys we should emit (for dashboards and auto-triggers): `feature.rollout.cohort`, `fallback.reason` (e.g., capacity|latency|error), `post_fallback.model_variant`, `latency.delta.p95`, `5xx.count`. make sure all are tagged with region + customer_id.

jess: add one more: `runtime.batch_size` and `queue.depth` — we saw unusual queueing last time during fallbacks.

mike: small ask on the rollout logic: client-side cohorts are sticky, but server may reassign if region goes unhealthy. propose server-reassign only when > 60% of requests from cohort in a region fail fallback checks for 2m. this reduces churn.

eric (pm): launch gating (hard): no increase to 5xx > 1.5% within first 24h in any region, and p99 latency regression < 20% averaged over 3h. soft gates: user-reported quality regressions triaged within 4h.

alina: SDK changes + docs needed: flag rollout API + stable cohort hashing example + migration guide (old flag -> new). I'll create a PR for SDK later today.

mike: putting the deploy config in the k8s canary job — will attach SHA/commit in the deploy message once staged. sample command: `rctl rollout start --flag rlw.regional_fallback_v2 --sequence seq.json`

deploy-bot: [info] canary job queued for us-west-2 group A — no traffic until manual unpause. job_id=cb-20260318-42

eric (pm): next steps: 1) SDK PR (alina) 2) SRE runbook updates + auto-shred config (jess) 3) rollout sequence YAML (mike) 4) telemetry dashboards + alerting (sam). target: start canary tomorrow EOD.

alina: ack, will do SDK PR today.

jess: will draft runbook and emergency steps, include rollback playbook and customer comms templates.

mike: will upload sequence and initial seq.json to the infra repo, link when ready.

sam: I'll wire dashboards and create an experiment id for A/B tracking (exp_id=exp-rlw-2026-03).

eric (pm): thanks all — will open a follow-up thread with exact timestamps and the manual unpause checklist. :thumbsup:
